title: Appeals and Grievances Compliance Standard on Overturned Decisions and Non-Retaliation
content:
Once an **Appeals and Grievances** case overturns or partially overturns a decision, the plan owes the obligations below; members who file are protected throughout.

## Standard

When a decision is overturned or partially overturned, the plan authorizes or provides the disputed service within the case type's effectuation period in hours of the resolution and pays for services continued during the case. No action is ever taken against the member for filing where the case type prohibits it, as every case type does.

## Effect on the records at resolution

| Resolution of the case | Subject of the case | Booked on resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Overturned or partially overturned | Prior authorization denial | An approval of the authorization under Prior Authorization, with the decision date equal to the resolved date and the request recorded as a provider request |
| Overturned or partially overturned | Pharmacy exception denial | An approval of the exception under the Pharmacy Benefit, dated the resolved date |
| Upheld | Any | Neither approval |

## Points of judgement

- **Partial overturn.** A partial overturn carries the same obligation as a full overturn: the disputed service is authorized or provided within the effectuation period, and continued services are paid for.
- **Counting the effectuation period.** The period runs in hours from the resolution of the case.
- **Filing is protected.** Filing a grievance, appeal, hearing request or external review is never a ground for any action against the member.

## Hypothetical illustration

A Standard Appeal about a prior authorization denial is resolved partially overturned on a given day. The authorization is booked as approved with that resolved day as its decision date, the plan authorizes or provides the disputed service within the effectuation period of the resolution, and it pays for the services continued while the appeal was pending.
